nit, please put a real address in here.  FF isn't a valid 7 bit address.

change to "ReadOffset"

Is there a way we can not make these required?  I believe SMBPBI has known indexes, we could access by a named enum to simplify?

Need a better type name here.  "Sattelite" is already taken by redfish aggregation, which it really shouldn't have been (it's on my list to propose a better name), but here we are.

SMBPBI probably?
Lets go with SMBPBI_VEEPROM, just to differentiate from other smbpbi stuff.

This really shouldn't be a template.  We should have one method that reads in a byte array, then we can have two methods that convert that byte array into the type (double or uint64_t)

As written this duplicates a bunch of code that's common between the two templates.

Is there a reason to be using the raw i2c device rather than an eeprom?  The SMBPBI protocol is effectively a virtual eeprom.  The really nice thing with using the eeprom interface is you can easily write test cases against it (because you can create a fake blob and/or file to test against.)

I don't know of a particular reason why this was chosen, but I know that this works without a driver and without consuming the bus and address.

I suspect you're right, it could use an eeprom in the future.  Not sure we need that in this commit?

Please don't do this.

I don't know why it is necessary for `open`.  If we can only make `ioctl` work with these, I'd suggest we write a small wrapper function so we only need the NOLINT once.
I suspect this can be made common in the RAII class proposed below.
Can we use a RAII class for this?

This is doing IO within the main loop, which will result in DBus blocking for some amount of time......  I'm not sure how to solve that with the way this is structured, but this will cause slow sensor APIs.
I don't think this is safe between architectures, right?
power is 4B according to spec, I think it's handled in `reading2power`, please correct me if I'm wrong
You can't just cast a uint8_t[4] to an int 64.  It works in this case becasue we're matching endianness, but that's not gauranteed.
Understood. Do we agree that it's being handled in this case or something more required here?
PLDM?  What is this function doing.
+1.  I really suspect this is just named poorly.
same as above, this type probably needs a better name.
This whole lambda needs to be rolled into a method, per the coding standard.
Same here.  This lambda is way too big.
I think there's a helper function for this now?  Check utils.
I don't see one for starting a timer and setting up the sensor, can you please link if possible?
This needs to be rebased and reworked on top of master, as the source tree structure has been changed.
Not sure what this does, and doesn't look like part of the build, remove.
nit, can you put this comment on another line.
These should probably go in the cpp file to be consistent.

There is another set of review for adding support for SmbpbiSensor.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/q/topic:%22smbpbi%22
We would want to be combine or pick one. 
IMO this patch is more consisting with existing dbus-sensor services
I'll abandon the changes I have out for review, I'm fine with this implementation!
there's a utility function for this (look at external sensor for an example).  Just lower casing the type is incorrect for types like fan_tach, and doesn't handle errors properly.

`getPathForUnits` is used in external to convert Units to interface name
https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/4bbd02dce8fe574ecae5efda089e02940178cac7/src/external/ExternalSensor.cpp#L42

Did you mean some other util?

Lets make this not a template, and separate it into two functions:
1. a function that reads the i2c value in an array of bytes
2. two functions that converts to the appropriate types.

as-is, 90% of this function is common, but will be duplicated anyway because this is a template.
nit, this is c++, we'd generally have this as a reference.
I think you're looking at an older patchset - pathset4 has a ref
nit, this should go on its own line.
nit, you're in a block comment here, there's no need for prefixed "* "
whitespace problems.  just make sure your meson is up to date, and run "meson format -i <this filename>" and it'll format for you.

"SMBPBI" or "SMB-PBI"?  Can we avoid RanDOmcAse for an acronym?

https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/d886ce89fe66c128b3ab492e530ad48fa0c1b4eb/cpp-style-and-conventions.md?plain=1#L281
SmbpbiEeprom is what we would use to match camel case with the other EM types.
(Seems like outstanding feedback is still unaddressed anyhow.  Didn't do a very exhaustive review of this revision.)
Why do we have this if we have SPDX?
it's something that's part of our process.  If it matters we can change it, but might take some time.
Who's process?  Most files in the openbmc org don't have any copyright notice at all.

sorry, should've specified.  Nvidia process for new files in open source (we have internal CI checks).  Intel had a very similar requirement which resulted in much the same in other files in this repo:

https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/adc/ADCSensor.cpp#L1


FWIW, I'd rather openbmc just document that SPDX will be accepted and nothing else, but I don't think we're there in terms of consistency.

nit, if you just named this "raw" or "data" it would probably all fit on one line and be more readable.

Up to you if you want to change

need to use memcpy_s here per secure coding rules.

use sizeof(reading) and length as your two length things.
NVM, looks like we don't have memcpy_s in here yet.... not sure why.

nit, can we explicitly call this DOUBLE64 ?  Or FLOAT64?  That makes it a lot more clear what the type is.

looking at what packages like numpy do here: https://numpy.org/doc/2.1/reference/arrays.scalars.html#numpy.float64

Pretty sure this needs updated to match

Float64
Float32
Int32
Int64

"Raw" and "Double" don't make a lot of sense in the config.

I think we should leave this as Raw and Double because some sensors require SMBPBI decode. 
The `Double` sensors can directly be read as DOUBLE64, but some `Raw` sensors (temp) require conversion. We handle this based on spec in `readRawEEPROMData` from `Units` instead of leaving it to the user.
Renamed Raw to UINT64 and Double to FLOAT64
This was changed to `SMBPBI_VEEPROM` (all caps) in a previous patchset to maintain naming convention
This looks duplicated now.  Should only need one.
nit, these two are the same.
potential out of bound? There is no checking on size of raw
The only place it is called from refers to it as a 8B uint. We only care about the first 4 bytes in SMBPBI
Is the data format timed to data type, for example power vs temperature? Are the format part of a standard/spec? Please add comments of what the data format is to help reviewer of the code.
clear all bits of tempd before the loop
Sorry, did not finish my comment earlier. What if 0 is a valid reading?
0 could be valid, invalid is all 0xff's.
What I meant is reading will be set 0 when all bytes are 0xff (data is not available) or the actual data bytes are 0 (valid reading of 0). How would one tell there is no valid reading?
is FLOAT32 not supported? It is defined in the enum class
At the moment we only need to read 8 bytes at a time

Please consider use more descriptive names for these functions.
For example i2cReadDataBytes() describes the function better than i2cCmd()
How is this different than name in base class Sensor?
I feel a lot of them can be moved to private
Which ones? The variables are used to create sensor callbacks. Moved methods to private.
Does the function only work with EEPROM?

This function is confusing:
1. Why is it static?
2. Why it just returns parameter? Whereever it is used, why not use offset directly?
3. offset ins uint16, return value is uint8, it is going to be "truncated"

I agree this is confusing.
In a different implementation, it was being used to map offset to sensor reading length through a csv/config. This is not required anymore since we read blocks of 8bytes. The temp/power functions internally handle decode. Refactored to not use `getLength()`
I am not I see the advantage of using the random access file since only synchronized ioctl calls are being used with the patch. Is there a plan to use some of the asynchronized feature?
The plan is to move to async at some point. For now this is used to satisfy RAII for file handling.
can we make this consistent with other sensor service use pollRateMs or pollRateSecond so it is clear the unit of this variable
Sorry for the delay, I was occupied with other priorities
stored in a new variable, better for readability per comment above this line
static assert also? or imply use "length=sizeof(reading)"
return ret; I think it is better to keep the return code
i think "convert2Temp" describe better of what the function does.
same here convert2Power() is a better name IMO
Looks like this should be voltage - I would add a comment to clarify what sensorType is expected here in else{}
valueType FLOAT32 is also defined in hpp. If it is not supported, please remove from the enum
Float32 is valid per spec, we do not use it in our current implementation so will leave it in for clarity
also, i am wondering if it is better to check the valid valueType when creating the sensor. This can potentially flood the journal log
should this be size_t based on how this is used
duplicate of base class member, remove
This should be enabled or unspecified by default.  We can remove it in the PACKAGECONFIG on the yocto side.  That way we get compile testing of your code.
All dbus-sensors daemons are set up to execute from /usr/bin, I think it'll be cleaner to change all of them in another patch?
Is checkInvalidReading() needed for UI64 also?
Yes, it is done in `readRawEEPROMData` on L287 since we need to return a double.
All my comments have been addressed
